patient.name: Nadia Rahman
patient.setting: GP surgery, then breast one-stop clinic
patient.complaint: Tender lump in the right breast that seems bigger before her period
background: Periods regular but heavier this year
Two children, breastfed both; youngest is 9
No family history of breast cancer
Pharmacist in Tower Hamlets; no regular medication

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' with a smooth, tender, mobile lump in a woman of 30 to 50 that changes with her cycle, against fibroadenoma (younger, non-tender), galactocele (after breastfeeding) and cancer (hard, fixed, skin changes).

points: Nadia, 44, found a **tender** lump in her right breast.
It gets **bigger and sorer before her period**, then eases.
Some general breast aching on both sides.
No nipple discharge, no skin change.

steps.lead: Nadia is **44 and still having periods**: the peak age and hormonal state for breast cysts.

visual.title: Age and breast lumps
visual.label: Nadia 44
visual.caption: Cysts cluster at **30 to 50**, especially around the perimenopause.

points: Right upper outer quadrant: **2.5 cm smooth, well-defined** lump.
It is **mobile**, slightly tender and feels fluctuant.
No skin tethering, no nipple change, no axillary nodes.
A smaller, similar lump in the left breast.

steps.lead: Nadia's lump is classic: **smooth, mobile, well-defined, tender**, cyclical, and there may be more than one.

visual.title: Nadia's lump across her cycle
visual.caption: Larger and more tender in the **luteal phase**, before her period.

steps.lead: Nadia's lump is a **fluid-filled sac** from a blocked duct, part of benign **fibrocystic change**.

steps.q: Which feature would make you worry that Nadia's lump is cancer rather than a cyst?
o: Change in size with her cycle
steps.r: A **hard, irregular, fixed** lump, skin change or nodes are red flags. Tenderness, multiple lumps and cyclical change fit a cyst.

steps.lead: Nadia stopped breastfeeding 9 years ago, so a **galactocele** is unlikely, and she has **no red flags** for cancer.

steps.title: Smooth breast lumps: which one?
head: Lump
Age

Clue
rows: Varies with cycle; may be multiple

steps.text: 'Smooth and mobile' alone does not mean cyst: a fibroadenoma is too. **Tenderness, fluctuation, cyclical change and age 30 to 50** point to a cyst.

investigation.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate investigation?' where the answer is breast ultrasound (shows a fluid-filled lesion) as part of triple assessment, with aspiration to confirm and relieve it.

points: Nadia is referred to the breast one-stop clinic.
Every new discrete breast lump has **triple assessment**.
At 44, imaging starts with ultrasound of the lump.

steps.q: Which imaging is the key test for Nadia's lump?
steps.r: **Ultrasound** tells fluid from solid at once. MRI and PET are not first-line for a lump.

steps.title: Nadia's breast ultrasound
steps.text: A **simple cyst**: thin wall, all fluid, nothing solid.

steps.lead: Nadia's ultrasound shows a **fluid-filled lesion**; **ultrasound plus aspiration** is the gold standard.
Because Nadia's cyst is sore, **fine needle aspiration** confirms it is a cyst and relieves her symptoms in one go.

steps.title: Nadia's work-up
nodes: Simple cyst and no symptoms → reassure
Thick, solid or residual mass → imaging and biopsy

steps.text: Ultrasound is the imaging of choice under 40 and the key test for a cyst at any age: it separates **fluid** from **solid** in seconds.

management.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate management?' where a simple asymptomatic cyst needs reassurance only, a painful cyst needs ultrasound-guided aspiration, and thick or solid aspirate or a residual mass needs imaging and biopsy.

steps.q: Nadia's large cyst is painful. What is the most appropriate management?
steps.r: A **symptomatic** cyst is drained by **ultrasound-guided FNA**. Reassurance alone is for asymptomatic simple cysts.

steps.lead: Nadia's right cyst is drained under ultrasound for **symptom relief**.

visual.title: Nadia's right cyst after aspiration
visual.caption: The cyst disappears completely: a reassuring sign. A small recurrence at 6 months is common.

steps.lead: Nadia's small left cyst is simple and painless, so she needs **reassurance only**.

points: The lump disappears completely after drainage.
No residual mass on repeat ultrasound.

steps.lead: Nadia's aspirate was clear, so she is **followed up for recurrence**; cysts that keep coming back are re-imaged and may be re-aspirated.
Had Nadia's aspirate been **thick** or the cyst had **solid elements** or a mass left behind, she would need imaging and **biopsy**.

steps.text: Do not refer a simple cyst for **excision**. Surgery is not the answer; aspiration is for symptoms, and biopsy only for suspicious features.

science.exam: Expect applied questions on why cysts change with the menstrual cycle, why they peak in the perimenopause, or what the aspirate tells you.

steps.lead: Nadia's cyst is a **dilated terminal ductal-lobular unit**, filled with fluid as part of fibrocystic change.

steps.title: How a breast cyst forms
nodes: Overgrowth of glandular and connective tissue
Terminal ductal-lobular unit dilates with fluid

steps.lead: Nadia's lump swells before her period because **oestrogen and progesterone** rise and fall through the cycle.

steps.q: Why are breast cysts most common in women Nadia's age?
o: Breast tissue is replaced by fat
steps.r: **Perimenopausal** hormone swings are the biggest. After menopause, cysts become uncommon.

steps.lead: Nadia is **perimenopausal**, when the hormonal swings are greatest; once her periods stop, new cysts become less likely.
Draining Nadia's cyst **decompressed** it and stopped the pain, and the **clear** fluid was reassuring.

steps.text: A new cyst in a postmenopausal woman not on HRT is unusual: think harder about other causes and image carefully.

glossary.Breast cyst: Benign fluid-filled sac in breast tissue, common in women aged 30 to 50.
glossary.Simple cyst: Thin-walled, fluid-only cyst with no solid part on ultrasound; benign.
glossary.Fibrocystic change: Benign hormone-related lumpiness and cysts in the breast.
glossary.Terminal ductal-lobular unit: The milk-producing lobule and its small duct, where cysts form.
glossary.Galactocele: Milk-filled cyst in a woman who has recently stopped breastfeeding.
glossary.Fibroadenoma: Benign firm, rubbery, very mobile, non-tender lump in young women.
glossary.Breast mouse: Nickname for a fibroadenoma because it slips away under the fingers.
glossary.Fluctuant: Feels like fluid under pressure when pressed.
glossary.Mobile: Moves freely under the skin and over deeper tissue.
glossary.Premenopausal: Still having periods, before the menopause.
glossary.Perimenopause: The years around the menopause when hormone levels swing most.
glossary.Luteal phase: Second half of the menstrual cycle, after ovulation, when progesterone is high.
glossary.Oestrogen: Main female sex hormone; stimulates breast glandular tissue.
glossary.Progesterone: Hormone of the luteal phase that also acts on breast tissue.
glossary.Triple assessment: Clinical examination, imaging and needle sampling of a breast lump.
glossary.Breast ultrasound: Imaging with sound waves; shows whether a lump is fluid or solid.
glossary.Anechoic: Black on ultrasound because it contains fluid that reflects no echoes.
glossary.Posterior acoustic enhancement: Bright area behind a fluid-filled lesion on ultrasound.
glossary.FNA: Fine needle aspiration: drawing fluid or cells out with a thin needle.
glossary.Fine needle aspiration: Thin needle draws out cyst fluid or cells; confirms and treats a cyst.
glossary.Aspirate: The fluid or cells drawn out by a needle.
glossary.Aspiration: Draining fluid with a needle and syringe.
glossary.Ultrasound-guided: Using ultrasound to place the needle accurately.
glossary.Core biopsy: Wider needle sample of tissue for histology.
glossary.Residual mass: A lump still present after a cyst has been drained; needs biopsy.
glossary.Red flags: Features suggesting cancer: skin changes, hard irregular mass, lymphadenopathy.
glossary.Lymphadenopathy: Enlarged lymph nodes, such as in the axilla.
glossary.Skin tethering: Skin pulled inwards over a lump, a sign of cancer.
glossary.One-stop clinic: Breast clinic where examination, imaging and biopsy happen in one visit.
glossary.Breast abscess: Collection of pus in the breast, usually when breastfeeding, with fever.
